content.paragraph: We know from Section 17.1 how to solve the complementary equation. (Recall that the solution is $$y_{c} = c_{1}y_{1} + c_{2}y_{2}$$ , where $$y_{1}$$ and $$y_{2}$$ are linearly independent solutions of Equation 2.) Therefore Theorem 3 says that we know the general solution of the non-homogeneous equation as soon as we know a particular solution $$y_{p}$$ . There are two methods for finding a particular solution: The method of undetermined coefficients is straightforward but works only for a restricted class of functions $$G$$ . The method of variation of parameters works for every function $$G$$ but is usually more difficult to apply in practice.
